items.body: Register Login Ducks Activate Ian Moore From Injured Reserve By Bradley Keith | at November 15, 2026 9:05 pm Anaheim’s Ian Moore has finally made his season debut tonight against Calgary, as the club shared that he was activated shortly before puck drop. Going down with a lower-body injury back in September, the 24-year-old had been thought to be on the shelf for around 2-4 weeks, but instead he has missed the first 20 games of the campaign. He resumed skating late last month and now embarks on his second full-time NHL season, needing 30 more appearances to meet the 100-mark. The defenseman was chosen 67th overall in the 2020 draft by Anaheim, turning pro after a four-year career at Harvard where he wore the “C”. Skating in 67 games last year where he chipped in 12 points on 13:40 a night, Moore started 54% of his five-on-five shifts in his own end making the most of his 6’3″ frame by blocking 80 shots. The righty is still looking to smooth out other aspects of his game, however, finishing as a -14 with a 38.7% on-ice Goals% at even strength. Back in June the Salt Lake City native earned a two-year extension worth $2.3MM per season. It was a tumultuous off-season for GM Pat Verbeek , having to make uncomfortably large commitments to his young players while several veterans were forced out, with a mass exodus on the back end. None of those contracts surpass that of the record-setting deal with center Leo Carlsson , although in plenty of ways, Moore has his own pressure and expectations to help bring stability behind star #1 Jackson LaCombe . A typical stay-at-home player, Moore has an unusual role under head coach Joel Quenneville . items.title: Devin Cooley sees goaltending — and life — differently. Other pro goalies are starting to take notice.
items.summary: Cooley's viral interviews have sparked a larger conversation about pressure, perspective, and the mental demands of professional goaltending.
items.body: Cooley’s philosophical postgame quotes have captivated hockey fans, from his mantra of “Nothing matters. Nobody cares. We’re all going to die,” to the existential insight of “The past is dead. There’s nothing for you there.” Fans aren’t the only ones paying attention. Cooley’s fellow NHL goalies have been watching along as he delivers answers fresh off a motivational poster, offering an alternative to the bland quotes players are used to giving. “A lot of answers you see in a hockey locker room are pretty freaking boring and cliche,” Capitals goaltender Charlie Lindgren told RMNB. “There’s not much to it, it’s kind of the same old answers. Now he steps into the fold and completely different. “He’s obviously a very unique human being. I don’t know him personally, but you can just tell, the way he’s thinking and talking, he’s definitely more of a deep thinker, and he’s not going to give you the standard answers. He’s going to go out and be himself and answer the questions the way he wants to.” View this post on Instagram Becoming an “unconscious goalie” Cooley’s approach to goaltending, in particular, has struck a chord with his peers. He’s repeatedly emphasized the importance of, in effect, turning his brain off when he’s in net to let his instincts do the work. “The problem with me is that I have a lot of fun playing, but when I start having too much fun, it [changes me] from an unconscious goalie to a conscious goalie,” he told Sportsnet’s Brendan Parker last month. “And my conscious brain is really bad at playing goalie. items.title: Oilers’ McDavid ties Gretzky’s record for fewest games to record 40 assists
items.summary: Connor McDavid is showing shades of Wayne Gretzky once again.
items.body: Connor McDavid is showing shades of Wayne Gretzky once again. The Edmonton Oilers captain tied Gretzky's record for the fewest games to record 40 assists, doing so in his 22nd contest of the season against the Philadelphia Flyers on Sunday. McDavid took a pass from Leon Draisaitl in the slot and fed a backhand pass right back to his linemate for a one-timer power-play goal. It came one day after McDavid extended his point streak to a career-best 21 games and reached 50 points on the season with an assist to Evan Bouchard against the Maple Leafs on Saturday. However, the 29-year-old superstar is still far from that record. Gretzky holds the NHL record for the longest point streak at 51 games, which he set in the 1983-84 season with the Oilers. Gretzky piled up a ridiculous 61 goals and 92 assists over the 51-game streak, and went on to finish the season with 205 points. McDavid, now at 11 goals and 41 assists over his 22-game tear, is on pace for 199 points this season. Only Gretzky has ever surpassed the 200-point mark, a feat he accomplished four times over his career.

items.body: Register Login Lineup Notes: Heiskanen, Sharks, Gudas By Bradley Keith | at November 15, 2026 8:03 pm Dallas hopes Miro Heiskanen can return Tuesday in Vegas, Stars reporter and NHL.com correspondent Robert Tiffin reports . The elite defender hasn’t played since his upper-body injury sustained on November 3 against Washington, taking a hard hit from Justin Sourdif . Impressively, missing their #1 defenseman for the last four games, Dallas has picked up five out of a possible eight points including a shutout win over Buffalo yesterday. Speaking to the strength on their blueline, they’ve been in good hands leaning on the trio of Thomas Harley , Esa Lindell , and Nils Lundqvist . So far this season Lundqvist’s usage has surpassed the 18-minute mark, the highest of his career. Harley has also enjoyed a noticeable uptick, currently leading the team in average ice time at over 25 minutes a game. Prior to going down, the 27-year-old Heiskanen looked like his normal elite self with 11 points in 15 games, still ranked 13th in the league with his 24:53 of usage per game. Dealing with a major knee injury in the past, the Finn has mostly been durable, although he hasn’t gotten through a campaign without missing a single game since being a rookie eight years ago. Having to play without him again tonight against Florida, Dallas hopes he’ll be all set against the Golden Knights in the week ahead.

items.title: Rangers Move Igor Shesterkin To Season-Ending LTIR
items.summary: The New York Rangers have moved goaltender Igor Shesterkin to season-ending LTIR.
items.body: Register Login Rangers Move Igor Shesterkin To Season-Ending LTIR By Brian La Rose | at November 15, 2026 5:00 pm The Rangers have quietly made a move to open up considerably more salary cap flexibility. PuckPedia reports ( Twitter link ) that the Rangers have transferred goaltender Igor Shesterkin from regular LTIR to season-ending LTIR. The placement means that the netminder won’t be able to return at any point in 2026-27, either in the regular season or the playoffs. Considering he was ruled out for the season when he sustained a leg injury last month, the Rangers aren’t really taking any sort of risk making this move. When a player goes on regular LTIR, the cap flexibility created is capped at the lower of the player’s AAV or last year’s average salary, roughly $3.9MM this season. That amount is also reduced by the amount of regular cap space the team has at the time. This is the route New York initially took, giving them ample flexibility to recall Dylan Garand at the time of the injury and make other needed roster moves as well. However, when a player is moved to season-ending LTIR, the player’s full cap hit becomes spendable again, minus any existing cap room or existing LTIR usage. That’s especially notable when you consider that Shesterkin has the highest cap hit for a goalie in NHL history, checking in at $11,567,857. Per PuckPedia , the Rangers now have roughly $9MM in LTIR room at their disposal after today’s acquisition of Arvid Soderblom . They technically didn’t need to make this move to facilitate the trade as they had nearly $3MM in regular LTIR room beforehand and Soderblom only cut down about half of that. items.summary: Soderblom was recently put on waivers by Chicago after a tough start to the 2026-27 season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images A couple of small-time backstops are switching places. On Sunday, the Chicago Blackhawks acquired goaltender Spencer Martin from the New York Rangers . In exchange, the Rangers are receiving fellow backstop Arvid Soderblom. It’ll be a fresh start for Soderblom, who has seemingly fallen out of favor in the Windy City. He started the 2026-27 season with the Hawks, serving as the backup behind Spencer Knight. However, while the Blackhawks have struggled as a whole, Soderblom’s play has been anything but up to par. In five appearances so far, including four starts, the 27-year-old has allowed 21 goals, giving him a 4.67 goals-against average and a .842 save percentage, along with a 0-3-1 record. It led to Soderblom being placed on waivers last Sunday, with the Swedish backstop clearing on Monday. Chicago then sent him down to its American Hockey League affiliate, the Rockford IceHogs. He has played two games with the IceHogs, going 2-0-0, with a 0.99 GAA, a .957 SV% and one shutout. In 117 NHL games, Soderblom has a record of 25-68-15, with a 3.65 GAA, a .885 SV% and one shutout. He’s in the final season of his two-year contract extension, which he signed in July 2025. The deal carries an AAV of $2.75 million. Martin started this season with the Rangers’ primary affiliate, the Hartford Wolf Pack. However, with injuries to both Joonas Korpisalo and Igor Shesterkin, the 31-year-old was called up to the big club. items.title: Canadiens’ Josh Anderson, Mike Matheson to miss time with lower-body injuries
items.summary: Matheson had just came back to the lineup after missing six games due to injury.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images Some toughs coming out of La Belle Province. On Sunday, the Montreal Canadiens announced that forward Josh Anderson and defenseman Mike Matheson are both expected to miss at least a couple of weeks due to lower-body injuries. Anderson has been placed on injured reserve, meaning he only needs to sit out a week’s worth of action. However, the Canadiens stated that the 32-year-old is set to miss 3-4 weeks due to the ailment. It isn’t quite clear what has knocked Anderson out of action. He was in the lineup on Saturday night, when the Canadiens fell to the Colorado Avalanche , 4-1. He logged just 10:46 of ice time, the least amount of time from any Montreal skater. He was in action throughout the entire game, registering a plus/minus of -2, while putting a shot on goal and delivering three hits. In 19 games so far this season, the Burlington, Ont. native has posted eight goals and four assists for 12 points, sitting tied for second on the team in goals and fifth in overall scoring. Matheson returned to the lineup last Thursday night against the Boston Bruins , after missing the previous six games due to injury. It seemed like an average night for the 32-year-old, who picked up an assist in a 5-2 victory, registering 21:11 of ice time. However, whatever seems to be bugging him was enough to keep him out of the lineup on Saturday, with the Canadiens stating that Matheson will miss another 2-3 weeks with the injury. Matheson has appeared in just nine games thus far, posting a goal and four assists for five points. The Canadiens (12-4-4) sit in a three-way tie for first place in the Atlantic Division with the Tampa Bay Lightning and Ottawa Senators.

items.summary: Forward Josh Anderson will be out for three to four weeks, and defenceman Mike Matheson will miss two to three weeks, both with lower-body injuries, the Canadiens announced on Sunday.
items.body: The Montreal Canadiens will be without a pair of veterans for the foreseeable future. Forward Josh Anderson will be out for three to four weeks, and defenceman Mike Matheson will miss two to three weeks, both with lower-body injuries, the Canadiens announced on Sunday. Anderson, 32, appeared to have sustained the injury against the Colorado Avalanche on Saturday when he played a season-low 10:46 of ice time. Matheson returned for the Canadiens' game against the Boston Bruins on Thursday, playing 21:11, after being out since Oct. 27. The left-shot blue-liner has been in and out of the lineup with a lower-body injury since Oct. 10. Through 117 career NHL appearances, he has a 3.65 GAA with an .885 SV%. Those numbers aren’t great by any stretch but it’s worth noting that he was playing behind a team mired in a long-term rebuild. Soderblom’s best year came back in 2024-25 when his SV% checked in at .898. That was enough for GM Kyle Davidson to sign him to a two-year, $5.5MM contract to continue in the backup role. items.title: Avalanche claim Mike Reilly off waivers from Hurricanes
items.summary: Reilly has appeared in just eight games this season, but has some significant experience in the NHL.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images A veteran rearguard is heading to the Mile High City. On Sunday, the Colorado Avalanche claimed defenseman Mike Reilly off waivers from the Carolina Hurricanes . Reilly was put on waivers on Saturday, as the Hurricanes needed to make room for captain Jordan Staal , who was returning to the lineup after being activated from injured reserve. The 33-year-old has only been in the lineup sparingly since the puck dropped on the new campaign. Reilly has appeared in just eight games thus far, last appearance in the lineup on Oct. 18 in a loss to the Calgary Flames. He has yet to find the back of the net, but has registered two assists, a plus/minus of +4, while averaging 12:26 of ice time. It comes after he played 42 games for Carolina last season, including twice in the Stanley Cup Playoffs, as the Canes went on to win the franchise’s second championship. The Chicago native was chosen by the Avs has they have a noticeable hole on the blue line. The team announced on Saturday that star rearguard Cale Makar will be out a couple of weeks due to a lower-body injury suffered in a game against the Ottawa Senators last Thursday. Reilly might not have nearly the same level of talent that Makar has, but he can hold his own for the duration of the former’s injury. In 468 regular-season games in the NHL, Reilly has scored 19 goals and 116 assists for 135 points, including eight points in 23 postseason contests. He’s on a one-year, two-way contract that he signed in September. The deal carries an NHL cap hit of $850,000 and a minor-league salary of $450,000. items.summary: Nathan MacKinnon will be out one month, and Cale Makar will be sidelined two weeks, Colorado Avalanche coach Jared Bednar announced before their 4-1 win against the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday.
items.body: Nathan MacKinnon will be out one month, and Cale Makar will be sidelined two weeks, Colorado Avalanche coach Jared Bednar announced before their 4-1 win against the Montreal Canadiens on Saturday. Each sustained a lower-body injury in the second period of a 4-3 overtime loss to the Ottawa Senators on Thursday. MacKinnon's last shift came with 8:15 remaining in the second. The center grabbed his right side after attempting a reverse hit on Senators defenseman Artem Zub and stayed on the bench for a few minutes before heading down the tunnel. Makar took a shift at 10:44 of the second that lasted only four seconds before heading to the locker room. The defenseman briefly returned for a 23-second shift that ended with 5:20 remaining, but stayed on the bench for the rest of the period. The injury came four days after he left practice on Nov. 8 for precautionary reasons. "When I think about those two guys, it's like every matchup, they take it on, now someone else has to be able to step up and do that," Bednar said. "And then you are losing the depth down the lineup as you kind of do that because everyone is elevated." MacKinnon leads Colorado and is tied for fifth in the NHL with 30 points (10 goals, 20 assists) in 20 games; Makar is third on the Avalanche and tied for third among NHL defensemen with 23 points (five goals, 18 assists) in 19 games. "Probably the most important is the 5-on-5 offense that they create," Bednar said. "We can be playing an OK game, chances equal, tight game, and those guys, like the top players do, will find a way to make a play that's a difference-maker for you. Whether it's Cale or 'Mac,' or both of them combined, they generally win us a lot of hockey games because of that. So with out that, the rest of the game has to tighten up and get better.

items.title: Bill Watters, longtime NHL executive and broadcaster, dead at 83
items.body: Bill Watters, an NHL executive, player agent and Sportsnet broadcaster, has passed away. He was 83. Though Watters, of Orillia, Ont., became known for his work in hockey, he began his sports career as a football player, starring for the University of Toronto as a linebacker. He was then selected second overall by the Toronto Argonauts in the 1964 CFL draft, but never played a game after a knee injury in training camp. Watters went on to work with Hockey Canada as an assistant manager for the 1977 and 1978 world championships before joining the Toronto Maple Leafs as an assistant GM for 12 years beginning in 1991. "A longtime member of the team's front office, Bill was an important part of my time as a player with the Maple Leafs and someone I will remember with affection," Maple Leafs senior executive advisor of hockey operations Mats Sundin said Sunday. "Bill cared deeply about the Leafs, the City of Toronto, and the people around him. "On behalf of the Maple Leafs organization, I would like to express our sincere condolences to Bill's family, friends and everyone who had the privilege of knowing him. He will be missed." After his Leafs tenure ended, Watters turned to broadcasting, co-hosting Sportsnet's Hockey Central and Prime Time Sports on 590 The Fan upon its 1989 debut. Watters was also a player agent, representing Maple Leafs such as Rick Vaive.

The Pens currently sit second from the bottom in the Eastern Conference and 10 points out of a playoff spot, with a core who are all pushing 40 years of age. During a first-period power play for New Jersey, former Cap Connor Brown tied the game with what the NHL ruled was not a distinct kicking motion. With Brown at the netfront, Devils winger Jesper Bratt ferried the puck right to his skates, which sent the puck into the back of the net. Capitals fans were in uproar over the goal at Capital One Arena, and the NHL’s Situation Room deemed it borderline enough to warrant a video review. Ultimately, however, the goal stood. The guiding principle in this case is NHL Rule 37.4: Distinct Kicking Motion , which defines what counts as an illegal kick. Pucks are allowed to deflect off of skates and into the net, but a player who beats the goalie with a “distinct kicking motion” will have his goal overturned. After the video review, the Situation Room released a statement on their findings: Video review supported the Referee’s call on the ice that the puck deflected off Connor Brown’s skate and entered the net in a legal fashion. Rule 37.4 states, in part, “a puck that deflects into the net off an attacking Player’s skate who does not use a ‘distinct kicking motion’ shall be ruled a GOAL. Vezina turned to Canadiens coach Leo Dandurand, his companion on this impromptu scouting trip, and suggested that Hainsworth had the tools to be a good NHL goalie. He would offer more praise when he later played against Hainsworth in an exhibition game, the latter impressive once again, but little did Vezina know that he was anointing his own successor, Hainsworth skating into the Canadiens net for the first time 100 years ago tomorrow (Nov. 16, 1926). The Canadiens were desperate, Vezina having died of tuberculosis the previous March 27. Their superstar goalie played just 20 minutes of a single game in 1925-26, his illness leaving him too weak to continue that Nov. 28 night, the disease ultimately taking his life four months later. Given the choices for the top-hat and formal-gown set in the metropolis a century ago, that’s saying something. It was almost sidebar news that the Rangers, under coach Lester Patrick playing their first game in franchise history on Nov. 16, 1926, would defeat the Eddie Gerard -coached defending Stanley Cup-champion Montreal Maroons 1-0. Bill Cook , assisted by his brother, Fred (better known as Bun), scored the night’s only goal, bouncing a shot off the ear of Maroons goalie Clint Benedict at 18:37 of the second period. At the other end of Madison Square Garden ice, superb Hal Winkler was unbeatable in the Rangers net, stopping 48 shots to the 43 turned aside by Benedict. From left: Bill Cook, Frank Boucher and Fred “Bun” Cook were nicknamed as the A Line or Bread Line with the New York Rangers in the 1920s and 1930s. This undated photo was taken at Madison Square Garden in New York. The game featured another historical note: it included the participation of the Rangers’ Clarence “Taffy” Abel , by many reports the first player of Indigenous heritage to play in the NHL. They will practice in Columbus on Monday before departing. Waddell said Bowness will not accompany them but could join the team at some point during the trip if cleared to do so. “He’s doing OK,” Waddell said. “He’s just got some things that are affecting him that we need to figure out, the doctors need to figure out.” Bowness missed 11 games during the 2023-24 season as Winnipeg Jets coach. Nick Suzuki replied with a highlight-reel goal for Montreal (12-4-4), which had gone 12 consecutive games without losing in regulation (9-0-3). Svechkov opened the scoring on Colorado’s first shot at 3:57 of the first period. He held on to the puck on a two-on-one rush and beat Dobes for his third of the season. Nelson doubled the lead at 15:55 during a delayed Montreal penalty, rifling a one-timer from a tight angle for the Avalanche’s second goal on three shots. Suzuki cut the deficit with a spectacular goal at 10:25 in the second. The Canadiens captain received a pass from Juraj Slafkovsky in the slot, smoothly spun around Avalanche defenceman Devon Toews and flicked a backhand off the post and in for his eighth of the season. items.body: DALLAS — Dallas captain Jamie Benn scored a second-period goal during Saturday night’s game against the Buffalo Sabres for his 1,000th career NHL point, all with the Stars. Benn, 37, and in his 18th NHL season, is second to Hall of Famer Mike Modano (1,359) in career points for the franchise that began as the Minnesota North Stars in 1967 and moved to Texas in 1993. The Stars’ bench emptied to celebrate the moment when the longest-tenured captain in Stars history snapped a scoreless tie with his goal. Benn — a native of Victoria, British Columbia — was drafted in the fifth round in 2007 and made the Stars’ opening night roster in 2009, recording his first league point on an assist in his second game. He won the league’s 2014-15 Art Ross Trophy for leading the NHL with 87 points (35 goals, 52 assists). He scored a career-high 41 goals the following season, when he was selected for the second of his two All-Star teams. Benn’s 1,272 career regular-season games played are the most of any Stars skater since the team relocated to Dallas and ranks second in franchise history behind Modano’s 1,459. On a Saturday night with so many friends and family that are going to be here and my dad’s celebration. It really is an incredible night for us two and our family.” During player arrivals, Thomas sported Tkachuk’s No.7 Blues jersey. He lived with the Tkachuk family during his rookie season in 2019. Tkachuk played nine of his 18 NHL seasons with the Blues and retired with the team after the 2009-10 season. He also played six seasons for the Winnipeg Jets, who drafted him with the No. 19 pick in 1990 NHL Draft, and five seasons with the Phoenix Coyotes. Wayne Gretzky holds the NHL record for the longest point streak at 51 games, which he set in the 1983-84 season with the Oilers. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Pittsburgh’s Egor Chinakhov preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to Tommy Novak ’s goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 13:22 (6:38 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mark Scheifele has carved his name in the Winnipeg Jets’ record books. The forward earned his 930th point to become the Jets’ franchise leader in points after he scored against the Chicago Blackhawks Saturday afternoon. Scheifele passed Dale Hawerchuk, who recorded 929 points in his nine seasons with Winnipeg between 1981-82 and 1989-90. Scheifele finished the game with a goal and three assists for four points. The Jets would come back from a 4-0 deficit to win 5-4 in a shootout. The 33-year-old center now has seven goals and 19 assists for 26 points in 21 games this season. Now in his 16th NHL season, Scheifele, a native of Kitchener, Ont., has 379 goals and 554 assists for 933 points in 982 career regular-season games. He also has 26 goals and 23 assists for 49 points in 53 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. In October 2025, Scheifele passed Blake Wheeler as the all-time points leader in the second iteration of the Winnipeg Jets . Before the start of the 2026-27 season, the NHL announced they would consolidate the two versions of the club , which means the statistical achievements of both eras would be recorded together. The “new” Jets, or Jets 2.0, were originally known as the Atlanta Thrashers and played in the capital of Georgia between 1999 and 2011. It was bought by True North Sports & Entertainment, who relocated the team to Winnipeg. Once the second version of the Jets became official, the team selected Scheifele with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2011 NHL Entry Draft, becoming the first-ever player selected by Winnipeg 2.0.

items.body: Mark Scheifele broke the franchise's all-time scoring record on Saturday, notching a goal in the second period against the Chicago Blackhawks. Scheifele is now at 930 career points — all with Winnipeg — surpassing the Dale Hawerchuk's mark of 929 set with the first version of the franchise. The milestone comes after the NHL announced this summer that statistics from both versions of the Winnipeg Jets are now merged, something made possible after the Arizona Coyotes went dormant in 2024. Scheifele was the first-ever draft pick by the new Jets franchise after moving to Winnipeg from Atlanta in 2011. Since then, he has been a consistent offensive star over his 14 seasons, including scoring a career-high 103 points last season. This season, he had 22 points in 20 games entering action Saturday. Before being drafted by the Jets, Scheifele played under Hawerchuk when the Jets legend coached the OHL's Barrie Colts. The fourth time will be the charm as the team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve assigned the netminder to AHL Texas on a conditioning stint. The 25-year-old spent training camp with Dallas but was claimed off waivers by New Jersey at the end of training camp. Then, when the Devils acquired Connor Hellebuyck , they moved Poirier to Washington for a seventh-round pick. But when the Caps needed a roster spot, Poirier was the odd one out, being claimed again by Dallas. While teams that originally lose a player to waivers who ultimately reclaim him can then send that player to the minors (as long as they’re the only claiming team), that isn’t the case with Poirier thanks to the trade. The Capitals are now the team in that situation. Accordingly, the Stars find themselves in a spot where he has to stay on the NHL roster or be waived again. At that time, Washington could reclaim him and then if they’re the only team to do so, they could then send him to AHL Hershey. The conditioning stint is a short-term workaround to that. It can last for up to two weeks and Texas plays in seven games in that span. If Poirier got to play in four or five of those, that would allow them to work off some of the rust from not being in a competitive game since the preseason. items.body: Register Login Chris Kreider Out Six To Eight Weeks By Brian La Rose | at November 14, 2026 2:15 pm The Canadiens will find themselves without a veteran winger for a while. The team announced ( Twitter link ) that Chris Kreider will miss approximately six to eight weeks due to a lower-body injury. The injury was sustained in the third period of Thursday’s victory in Boston following a collision with Michael Eyssimont . Kreider stayed down for a few seconds and was eventually able to hobble off largely under his own power but was unable to put any weight on his left leg. Kreider is in his first season with Montreal after joining them as a free agent a little before training camp. He reached an agreement on a mutual contract termination with Anaheim, allowing him to hit the open market where he inked a one-year, $2.15MM deal with another $3.25MM in potential performance bonuses. The 35-year-old has played in 19 games this season, meaning he has already hit $2MM of his bonus, that coming at the 10-game mark. He has three goals and six assists in those contests despite a pretty big drop in ice time; after logging over 17 minutes per night last season, Kreider is at just 13:21 this year. The rest of his bonuses are tied to goal production with the first payout coming at 10 goals, then at 20, 30, and 40. It’s safe to say at this point that the last two aren’t going to happen while even reaching 20 tallies will be tricky. Montreal was already carrying two extra forwards on its active roster so it’s unlikely that they will turn to a recall from AHL Laval. items.title: Penguins Assign Ilya Solovyov To AHL
items.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins have assigned defenseman Ilya Solovyov to AHL Wilkes-Barre/Scranton.
items.body: Register Login Penguins Assign Ilya Solovyov To AHL By Brian La Rose | at November 14, 2026 12:50 pm The Penguins have made a roster move in advance of their game tonight against Ottawa. The team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve assigned blueliner Ilya Solovyov to AHL Wilkes-Barre/Scranton. The 26-year-old is in his first full season with Pittsburgh’s organization after being acquired back in January. However, while Solovyov was a full-timer on the NHL roster last season, that hasn’t been the case this year, as he cleared waivers last month and spent a bit of time in the minors. Solovyov played in three games with Wilkes-Barre/Scranton before getting the call back to Pittsburgh on October 18th. However, playing time has been rather scarce since then, as he has suited up for the big club just three times. This move was likely made for a couple of reasons. For starters, Solovyov hasn’t played since October 24th so simply getting him some playing time would be ideal. Additionally, his waiver exemption was starting to run low. Players who have cleared waivers can be on an NHL roster for 10 games or 30 days (whichever is reached first) before needing to clear again. Solovyov was only a handful of days away from the 30-day mark so by sending him down now, they avoid needing to run him through the waiver wire once again. With the assignment, Pittsburgh now has one open roster spot. With Trevor van Riemsdyk getting closer to returning, that spot may ultimately be ticketed for his activation from IR in the coming days.

items.body: The Minnesota Wild defenceman has been activated from the injured reserve and is set to make his season debut Saturday night against the Boston Bruins (Sportsnet+, 7 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PCT), the team announced . items.title: Stars Make Three Roster Moves
items.summary: The Dallas Stars have recalled defenseman Kyle Burroughs from AHL Texas and made two other roster moves on the back end as well.
items.body: Register Login Stars Make Three Roster Moves By Brian La Rose | at November 14, 2026 10:37 am The Stars have made a trio of roster moves heading into their game tonight against Buffalo. The team announced ( Twitter link ) that they have recalled defenseman Kyle Burroughs from AHL Texas. To make room on the roster, blueliner Lian Bichsel was placed on IR. To create the cap room needed for the recall, defenseman Kyle Capobianco was placed on LTIR. Burroughs is in his first season with Dallas after signing a one-year, two-way deal back in July. The 31-year-old has played exclusively with Texas so far, picking up five assists and 10 penalty minutes through 15 contests so far. Burroughs does have a fair bit of NHL experience under his belt, however. He was a full-timer on an NHL roster as recently as two years ago, when he had a full-time seventh role with Los Angeles, a year after playing in a career-high 73 games in San Jose. Overall, Burroughs has 22 points, 293 blocks, and 572 hits in 201 career NHL appearances. It wouldn’t be shocking to see Burroughs be in the seventh role while up with Dallas. That said, he could alternate with youngster Trey Taylor depending on the matchup as well. Bichsel’s IR placement should come as no surprise given that he received a week-to-week designation on Friday due to a lower-body injury. Meanwhile, Capobianco was placed on IR retroactive to October 27th, meaning he has already missed more than half of the 10-game, 24-day minimum absence for a player to be LTIR-eligible. The initial timeline was that he’d miss around four weeks with his leg injury so he may still be on track to return at the end of the month.

items.title: Canadiens’ Chris Kreider out 6-8 weeks with lower-body injury
items.summary: Chris Kreider has three goals and nine points in 19 games with Montreal in 2026-27.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Montreal Canadiens announced Saturday that forward Chris Kreider will be out for approximately six-to-eight weeks with a lower-body injury. The 35-year-old winger suffered the injury after Boston Bruins’ forward Michael Eyssimont slid into him during their game Thursday. Kreider went straight to the dressing room and did not return. In 19 games, Kreider has three goals and six assists for nine points. He signed a one-year, $2.15-million deal with Montreal in September after the Anaheim Ducks terminated his contract. In 2025-26, Kreider had 22 goals and 28 assists for 50 points in 75 games with the Ducks. He finished second on the team with eight power-play goals and reached the 20-goal mark for the eighth straight season. Through 15 NHL seasons, Kreider, a native of Boxford, Mass., has 351 goals and 290 assists for 641 points in 977 career regular-season games with the Canadiens, Ducks and New York Rangers . His best season came in 2021-22, when as a member of the Rangers, he scored 52 goals and finished with 77 points, both career highs. His 52 goals were third in the NHL that season. He was selected by New York with the No. 19 pick in the 2009 NHL Entry Draft. He was acquired by the Ducks after the 2024-25 season, with New York getting forward prospect Carey Terrance in return. The Canadiens are 12-3-4 with 28 points through their first 19 games of the 2026-27 regular season. Montreal will host the Colorado Avalanche on Saturday.

items.title: Maple Leafs’ Anthony Stolarz set for second straight start
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs are changing up their goalie rotation. Anthony Stolarz will make his second straight start Saturday when the team hosts the Edmonton Oilers (Sportsnet, Sportsnet+, 7 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PCT), head coach Jim Hiller told reporters . It will mark Stolarz's first back-to-back starts of the season. "He's been good for a long time. Not a lot of rebounds. Played well against Edmonton last time. A lot of different things," Hiller explained. Stolarz took the loss Thursday against the Minnesota Wild, coughing up four goals on 25 shots against. Over eight games this season, the 32-year-old holds a .900 save percentage and 2.90 goals against average — both superior numbers to Sergei Bobrovsky at .881 and 3.47 across 13 appearances. Stolarz led the Maple Leafs to a 7-2 win over Edmonton in October, stopping 30 of 32 shots against. Toronto is looking to snap a five-game losing streak and avoid a winless six-game homestand, while Edmonton is eyeing its fourth straight win.

items.title: Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness to miss second straight game
items.body: The Columbus Blue Jackets will be without their bench boss on Saturday. Coach Rick Bowness will miss his second straight game when his team hosts the Philadelphia Flyers, general manager Don Waddell told reporters . Bowness also missed Thursday's 3-1 loss to the Tampa Bay Lightning and was not present for practice on Friday or Saturday's morning skate. Waddell said Bowness, who was previously described as "under the weather," is "day-to-day," adding he would not coach practice Monday but could return Tuesday on the road against the New York Islanders. The 71-year-old coach is undergoing further testing for an issue he has been battling since Thursday morning. Assistant Don Granato, the former Buffalo Sabres head coach, took over for Bowness on Thursday will do so once again.

items.body: The Montreal Canadiens will be down a forward for the next while. Chris Kreider is expected to miss six to eight weeks with a lower-body injury the team announced on Saturday. In Thursday night's win against the Boston Bruins, Kreider was sent down the tunnel with less than 14 minutes remaining in the third period after Bruins forward Michael Eyssimont fell at the centre-ice line and slid into the veteran's knee. The 35-year-old Kreider stayed down on the ice after the awkward collision and officials whistled the play down almost immediately. He did not return to the game. Over 18 games this season, Kreider has tallied three goals and six assists. This is his first season with Montreal after joining the club on a one-year contract in September. He had played with the New York Rangers for the first 13 seasons of his career before suiting up for the Anaheim Ducks in 2025-26.

items.summary: There are 14 games on the NHL schedule for Saturday, including the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland, one broadcast nationally in the United States and three broadcast nationally in Canada. Here are five things to watch, along with the complete game schedule.
items.body: Avalanche's Burns to play 1,600th game; Ducks' Gauthier can stretch goal-scoring run There are 14 games on the NHL schedule for Saturday, including the 2026 NHL Global Series Finland, one broadcast nationally in the United States and three broadcast nationally in Canada. Here are five things to watch, along with the complete game schedule. Edmonton Oilers center Connor McDavid will put his 20-game season-opening point streak on the line in his hometown for Hockey Night in Canada showdown against the slumping Toronto Maple Leafs at Scotiabank Arena (7 p.m. ET; SNO, SNW, SNP, NHLN). McDavid is the fourth different player in NHL history with at least one point in each of the first 20 games of a season. Wayne Gretzky did it three times, including his record-51-game point streak to open the 1983-84 season. Mats Sundin (30 games, 1992-93) and Dany Heatley (22 games, 2005-06) are the others. McDavid leads the League with 49 points (11 goals, 38 assists). If he extends his point streak he will also become the fifth different player in NHL history to have 50 points by the 21st game of the season, joining Gretzky (three times), Mario Lemieux (three times), Bernie Nicholls and Mike Bossy . No one has done it since Lemieux in 1995-96. The Oilers (14-3-3) have won three straight, with points in 11 of 13 (9-2-2). It's the opposite for center Auston Matthews and the Maple Leafs (8-11-2), who have lost five straight games, all at home, by a combined 22-9. Salvaging a win in the finale of a six-game homestand would at least stop the bleeding. Toronto won 7-2 at Edmonton on Oct. 24, when forward William Nylander scored two goals. He has three in eight games since. This will also be Oilers coach Mike Babcock's first game in Toronto since being fired as Maple Leafs coach on Nov. 20, 2019.

items.body: Register Login Hurricanes Activate Jordan Staal, Place Mike Reilly On Waivers By Ryan Long | at November 14, 2026 9:34 am The Hurricanes will have their captain back for the second game of their Global Series set in Helsinki. Carolina announced it has activated Jordan Staal from injured reserve ahead of today’s game against the Kraken. To make room on the roster, the club placed defenseman Mike Reilly on waivers. Staal, 38, has missed the past 14 games after partially tearing his calf in warmups before an October 11 win in Philadelphia. Head coach Rod Brind’Amour originally said he’d be out one to two months, and Staal is back about a month later. He practiced with the team twice in Finland this week and worked on special teams Friday. He’s projected to center the third line between Seth Jarvis and Jordan Martinook . Staal had no points in six games before the injury, though he won 55.6% of his faceoffs and recorded 19 hits. He’s coming off a playoff run that ended with the Conn Smythe Trophy, eight goals and 12 points in 19 games, with six of those goals coming in the Final against Vegas. Reilly, 33, re-signed with Carolina in September on a one-year, two-way deal worth $850K in the NHL and $450K in the AHL. He came into the lineup after the Hurricanes lost their first two games, playing on the third pair with Shayne Gostisbehere and picking up two assists. He has been a frequent healthy scratch since mid-October. The 12-year veteran played 42 games for Carolina last season, with one goal, nine points and a plus-11 rating, and added two assists in two games during the Cup run. If he clears, the Hurricanes will send him to AHL Chicago.

items.title: Hurricanes activate Jordan Staal from IR, will return vs. Kraken
items.summary: Jordan Staal won the Conn Smythe Trophy in 2026 as he led the Carolina Hurricanes to their second Stanley Cup in franchise history.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Eric Bolte-Imagn Images The Carolina Hurricanes will soon get their captain back. The team announced Saturday that forward Jordan Staal has been activated off injured reserve and he will be available to play against the Seattle Kraken Saturday in Finland. Staal, 38, has been out of the lineup since he suffered a tear in his calf during the pregame warmups ahead of Carolina’s game against the Philadelphia Flyers Oct. 10. The six-foot-four center was pointless through his first six games this season but is coming up a 2025-26 campaign that saw him score 20 goals and add 16 assists for 36 points in 75 games. Staal led the Hurricanes to their second Stanley Cup championship in franchise history as he scored eight goals and added four assists for 12 points. He was awarded the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP. He signed a one-year contract extension in the offseason that will keep him with the team through the 2027-28 season. He has served as Carolina’s fulltime captain since 2019-20 after two seasons as co-captain with Justin Faulk. Staal, taken No. 2 overall by the Pittsburgh Penguins in the 2006 NHL Entry Draft, has 318 goals and 429 assists for 747 points in 1,409 career regular-season games with the Hurricanes and Penguins. He also has 46 goals and 39 assists for 85 points in 181 career playoff games. Along with his championship in 2026, Staal helped Pittsburgh win the Stanley Cup in 2009 and was part of their run to the Final in 2008.

But none of the 12 kids from the under-10 team Karpat club team based in Oulu were complaining Saturday, the day after their half-day trek. Because the payoff wasn’t a rec game in their municipal rink. It was the opportunity to meet Sebastian Aho of the Carolina Hurricanes at Veikkaus Arena, home of the 2026 NHL Global Series game between the Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken later Saturday (1 p.m. ET; HHN, Prime Video, CARNHL, KONG, KING, NHLN, SN1). Aho, who grew up in Oulu before charting a highlight-filled career in the NHL, joined the kids, who were selected through a random draw, after the Hurricanes held an optional morning skate. “(The kids) were asking some tricky questions and just having fun,” Aho said. “The parents had some nice questions where you are trying to send the message of just have fun and work hard and just love the game and everything else will take care of itself.” It was an important and valuable message, said Jyri Junnila, a coach in the program. "They were definitely nervous, as this was such a big event for them,” Junnila said. “The kids were a bit shy at first, but they eventually loosened up and even asked some questions.” The message resonates more strongly because it is the path that Aho followed in his journey to the NHL. Aho, who scored two goals in a 4-1 victory against the Kraken here on Thursday, says he knows the hopes and dreams of these kids. He says he has lived them. “Kind of surreal,” Aho said. “The whole week here, you see a lot of Finnish kids, you see Caniacs all the way from Raleigh. items.body: Register Login Kraken Activate Ryan Lindgren, Reassign Logan Morrison By Ryan Long | at November 14, 2026 8:03 am The Seattle Kraken have activated defenseman Ryan Lindgren from injured reserve, the team announced this morning. To make room on the roster, forward Logan Morrison has been reassigned to AHL Coachella Valley. Lindgren left Seattle’s October 6 game against the Vegas Golden Knights with an upper-body injury and was placed on IR two days later. At the time, he was given a four-to-six-week recovery window and returns after roughly five and a half weeks, just in time for Saturday’s Global Series finale against the Carolina Hurricanes in Helsinki. The former second-round pick had no points and a +3 rating through Seattle’s first four games before the injury. In the 13 games he has missed, the Kraken went 7-5-1 over that stretch to reach 9-7-1 overall. While the team overall has held their own over the last month, sitting just two points back of the third spot in the Pacific, his return could help steady a Seattle defense that has struggled without him. The Kraken entered the Global Series 29th in goals allowed per game and 31st on the penalty kill. Lindgren is in the second year of the four-year, $18MM contract he signed in free agency in July 2025. Morrison was called up on November 8 as extra forward depth for the trip to Finland. With only one game left before the Kraken head home, he goes back to the Firebirds, where he has three goals and nine points in 12 games this season. The 24-year-old led Coachella Valley with 61 points in 68 games last year. His only NHL experience is four games in 2023-24, and he is still looking for his first NHL point.

items.title: How we would fix the Chicago Blackhawks
items.summary: Blow it up? Fire the GM? Be more patient? What would you do?

Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images We had modest expectations at best for the 2026-27 Chicago Blackhawks . A look back at our predictions poll reveals none of us had them making the playoffs. But they did get some votes for fifth-, sixth- and seventh-place finishes in the Central Division. We at least expected progression. Instead, it’s been a season of regression. Despite having a comically loaded prospect pool and a strong crop of young NHL talent, the Hawks are a pitiful 31st in the overall league standings. It’s a mess for GM Kyle Davidson, who told reporters Wednesday he’s “looking to improve the playing roster,” implying he isn’t seeking futures. Let’s pretend the repair job is ours to tackle, Roundtable. How would you fix the Blackhawks? MATT LARKIN: I know the Bowen Byram trade already looks like a disaster but, oddly enough, I understood the philosophy behind it. It was the law of diminishing returns with all the prospects – you can only put so many in your lineup – and the Hawks needed someone to help them win the in present. While I’d clutch tightly to their 2027 first-round pick in hopes it gets them Landon DuPont, I’d be willing to part with other picks – they have eight in Rounds 1-2 this year – or some other good prospects in hopes of landing a prime-year forward who can help accelerate their timeline. The Hawks could further augment their roster next offseason with their gargantuan amount of 2027-28 cap space .
